text:
Connor Bedard missed the start of the season after shoulder surgery in the summer, came back into a team that then lost six straight, and spent this week being asked about his coach. He said the Blackhawks have "100 percent belief" in Jeff Blashill, as NHL.com put it in a headline.

His own play has held up. He has 15 points in 13 games (5 goals, 10 assists), and his goals sit right where his chances say they should: 5 on 5.5 expected. That is not a hot streak; it is roughly who he is. Our projection has him finishing between 68 and 96 points, 81 in the middle, if he plays every game from here.

The problem is the five-on-five picture. Chicago gets 43.2% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he faced top competition with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 91st percentile for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net. When the Blackhawks can get him the puck with speed, he still gets to the dangerous ice.
